author: Mark Atwood
text: API contract confidence: 30% chance of missed issue. Least confident flags: .12 (the serde_json type-leakage concern is real-engineering but argues against an already-decided workspace policy — marked opinion); .13 (docs-confusion severity is hard to estimate without telemetry on which field callers actually mis-use); .14 (the versioning note's actionable-vs-informational status depends on whether the workspace is positioning for a 1.0 cut soon — context I do not have). Highest confidence: .8 (duplicate-key footgun has a verified minimal repro that the crate's own from_str rejects), .9 (parent_id any-JSON acceptance was verified by reading the deserializer source), .10 and .11 are interlocked findings with the same evidence base (SetResponse pattern at jmap-types methods.rs:282 and Id contract at id.rs:20). Uncertainty driven by: (a) not surveying jmap-mail-server / jmap-mail-client to count actual callers of on_success_update_email and confirm the SemVer break in .14 hits real code in this workspace; (b) not running cargo public-api diff to enumerate the full SemVer-visible delta from 9c0d34f; (c) not checking whether SetError carries its own extra field that would catch vendor-error fields and partially compensate for the typed-up not_sent recommendation in .10; (d) not checking how parent_id three-way is consumed by jmap-mail-server's MailboxBackend impls — if backends already special-case non-spec values, the underspecification in .9 may be less acute than presented.
